passages.text: Every session should feel calm, clear and safe. The coach keeps the group moving at one steady pace.
A sample session has three phases: warm-up, main set and cool-down.
The practice station has a front rail, a sliding deck and a back step.
Resistance comes from colored bands. Green is light, blue is medium and red is heavy.
Sample Move A starts with both hands on the front rail and both feet on the sliding deck.
Sample Move A runs at a slow pace: four counts out and four counts back.
To make Sample Move A easier, shorten the range and keep one knee down.
Sample Move B starts standing on the back step, facing the rail.
The most common mistake in Sample Move B is rushing the return.
Tempo means how many counts each part of a move takes.
Range means how far the body travels in one move.
Set the pace first, then give the setup, and name the move last.
Keep cues short. One idea per cue is easier to follow than three.
If a client reports sharp pain, stop the move and offer an easier option.
Close the set with a clear finish so everyone knows the move is over.
